Antigen Recognition Molecules: Major 
Histocompatibility Complex (MHC)/Human 
Leukocyte Antigens (HLA)
Th e initiation of the immune response depends on our body’s
recognition of the “foreign” substance—the antigen. But how is 
this accomplished? In other words, how does our body distin-
guish self from non-self? Recognition of antigens is possible 
because our body’s cells are diﬀ erent from the antigen, and this 
diﬀ erence can be detected and communicated to other cells by 
a type of molecule referred to as the histocompatibility complex
